lines.text: אחז 34 אחי
adhering, these ideas being closely al-
lied; comp. לָכַד and לָקַח in Hithpa. and
ἔχομαι τινός to hold or depend from any
thing, ἐχόμενος joined with any thing;
also αἱρέω, whence Lat. hæreo.—Ez. 41,
6 וְלֹא יִהְיוּ אֲחוּזִים בְּקִיר הַבָּיִת that they
might not be joined to the wall of the
temple, i. e. inserted in it. 1 K. 6, 6.—
Hence
5. to make fast, to shut, e. g. to bar,
Neh. 7, 3. So Syr. ܐܶܚܰܕ.
6. to join together timber, to cover
with timber, beams, boards, etc. conta-
bulare. 1 K. 6, 10 and he covered the
house with cedar-wood. Comp. חָפַּשׁ
7. to take out or away, sc. from a larger
number; whence Part. pass. taken out,
taken, sc. from a lot or portion, (like sy-
non. נִלְכַּד,) Num. 31, 30 and from the
half which belongs to the children of Is-
rael, shalt thou take one [part] אָחוּז מִן
הַחֲמִשִּׁים taken from fifty. v. 47. 1 Chr.
24, 6 בֵּית־אָב אֶחָד אָחוּז לְאֶלְעָזָר וְאָחֻז אָחֻז
לְאִיתָמָר (where it should twice read
with many Mss. אֶחָד אָחוּז) one family
being taken for Eleazar, and one being
taken for Ithamar, i. e. in drawing lots
they drew first a lot for a family of Elea-
zar, and then one for a family of Itha-
mar.
Niph. 1. Pass. of Kal no. 2, Ecc. 9, 12.
2. Pass. of Kal no. 3, Gen. 22, 13.
3. to make oneself possessor of any
thing, to take or have possession, Gen.
Syr. ܐܶܚܰܕ to possess, and deriv. אֲחֻזָּה.
Piel to shut up, as Kal no. 5. Job
26, 9 shutting up the face of his throne,
i. e. veiling his throne with clouds.
Hoph. to be joined, fastened, to any
thing, pass. of Kal no. 4, 2 Chr. 9, 18.
Deriv. the six following.
אָחָז (possessing, possessor) Ahaz, pr.
n. m. a) A king of Judah, contemporary
with Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah, r. 744
—728 B. C. noted for his weakness of
character and idolatry, 2 K. 16, 1 sq. 2
Chr. 28, 16 sq. Is. 7, 1 sq. 38, 8. Sept.
אֲחֻזָּה f. (r. אָחַז Niph. no. 3) posses-
sion, espec. the possession of land,
fields, etc. Lev. 27, 24 לַאֲשֶׁר לוֹ אֲחֻזַּת
הָאָרֶץ to whom possession of the land be-
longed, i. e. who had been its owner.
v. 16. 21. 22. אֲחֻזַּת קֶבֶר possession of a
sepulchre, i. e. a sepulchre belonging to
a family, their own, Gen. 23, 4. 9. 20.
49, 30. In the connection אֲחֻזַּת נַחֲלָה
Num. 27, 7, and נַחֲלַת אֲחֻזָּה 35, 2. Spo-
ken of slaves Lev. 25, 45. 46.
אַחְזַי Ahzai, pr. n. m. Neh. 11, 13; for
which 1 Chr. 9, 12 יַחְזֵרָה. Prob. it
should read in both passages אֲחַזְיָה,
which see.
אֲחַזְיָה and אֲחַזְיָהוּ (whom Jehovah
holds) pr. n. Ahaziah. a) A king of Is-
rael, the son of Ahab and Jezebel, 897—
Ὀχοζίας. b) A king of Judah, the son
and successor of Joram, 884 B. C. 2 K.
אֲחֻזָּם (their possession) Ahuzzam,
pr. n. of one of the descendants of Ju-
dah, 1 Chr. 4, 6.
אֲחֻזַּת (possession) Ahuzzath, pr. n. of
a Philistine, the friend of king Abime-
lech, Gen. 26, 26.
* אָחַח a root not in use. I. Arab.
أَحْأَحَ onomatop. from the sound אָח
interj. to cry ah, ah, ah! repeatedly;
in Heb. perh. to sigh, to groan, to howl,
whence אֹחִים.
II. In Arabic also to be warm, hot, to
glow, sc. with anger, as in the words
أُحَاحٌ, أَحَاحٌ; whence perhaps may
be derived Heb. אָח, إِخٌّ, a pot, furnace.
Better however to derive the signif. fur-
nace from r. أَجَّ to flame, to burn, as fire,
Conj. II to kindle, أَجَّةٌ heat, etc. See
lett. ג.
אֲחֹחִי see אֲחוֹחַ.
אֲחִי (perh. apoc. from אֲחִיָּה) Ahi, pr.
אֲחִי see אֲחוּד.
אֲחִיאָם (for אֲחִיאָב father’s brother,
uncle) Ahiam, pr. n. m. 2 Sam. 23, 33.
אֲחִידָה Chald. i. q. Heb. חִידָה with
Aleph. prosthet. a riddle, enigma, Dan.

line_status.note: Final Syriac letter has the dot below (dalath, not rish) and the middle letter is a flat-topped heth, not semkath; the Syriac cognate of אחז is ܐܚܕ, matching Reading B.
The pe clearly has a dagesh dot inside it, and the dot over the final letter sits at its upper right, so it is shin not sin — matching Reading B.
The printed word has a vav with shureq dot between ḥet and zayin (אָחוּז, plene); there is no qibbuts under the ḥet, so Reading B's defective אָחֻז is wrong.
The first אָחוּז is printed plene with vav (shureq); only the two later forms וְאָחֻז אָחֻז are defective with qubbuts. Reading A wrongly made the first one defective.

The word nearest "Mss." (visually leftmost, so logically second) is printed plene אָחוּז with a vav+shureq, as in B; but the rightmost (logically first) word is אֶחָד, so the order is A's. A has the right order but wrong defective spelling (אָחֻז); B has the right spelling but reversed order.

The Arabic is the quadriliteral verb أَحْأَحَ: the print shows alif-hamza+fatha, ḥā with a sukūn (small circle), a second alif-hamza+fatha, and final ḥā with a single fatha — not a long ā nor a tanwīn as in Reading A.

The leftmost (first-read) Arabic word carries hamza + damma on the alif (a curled mark), while the second word, right of the comma, carries hamza + fatha (a flat stroke); both end in dammatan. Order damma-then-fatha matches Reading A.

The dot on the Arabic letter is printed above the stroke (خ, not ج below), and the superscript cluster shows shadda with dammatan, as in Reading A; Reading B has the wrong letter and drops the tanwin.

The third letter of the headword and the final letter of the reference word are both ח (no left foot as in ת), and the reference word ends with ח plus furtive patach directly before the period — no final yod is printed. Reading A matches; B's תַי is wrong.

Under the aleph of the cross-reference the print shows a vertical colon plus a short horizontal stroke (hataf patah, as under the aleph of the headword אֲחִי), not two side-by-side dots (tsere). Vav is printed plene with shureq; final letter is dalet.
